card.title: Animal Kingdom — Diagnostic Features and Classification

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Animals are sorted by how their bodies are built. Levels of organization climb from the protoplasmic grade of Protozoa through the cellular grade of sponges and the tissue grade of cnidarians to organ and organ-system grades. Symmetry runs from asymmetrical sponges through the radial cnidarians (secondarily radial adult echinoderms) to the bilateral plan of most animals.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Body cavity: Acoelom (no cavity) / Pseudocoelom (partly lined) / Coelom (fully mesoderm-lined)
Symmetry: Asymmetry (Porifera) / Radial (Cnidaria, Echinodermata) / Bilateral (Platyhelminthes onward)
Chordate features: notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Acoelomates have NO body cavity; pseudocoelomates have a cavity not fully lined by mesoderm; coelomates have a fully mesoderm-lined cavity.  ·  Cnidaria are radial (adult) but their larvae may be bilateral; echinoderms are radial in adults but bilateral in larvae (secondary radial symmetry).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the 9-phylum list with one class each and the body-cavity types.  ·  The 4 chordate features are a very common short-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Peripatus*** — connecting link between annelids and arthropods.  ·  ***Earthworm*** — true coelom and true metamerism.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Segmentation (metamerism) is seen in annelids, arthropods, and chordates — NOT in sponges or cnidarians.  ·  Porifera (sponges) have a cellular level of organisation (no true tissues); Cnidaria have tissue-level organisation.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Acoelomate flat, pseudocoelom round, coelomate segmented."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m): Distinguish diploblastic and triploblastic animals.** — Diploblastic animals (Cnidaria) have two germ layers, ectoderm and endoderm, separated by mesoglea; triploblastic animals have a third layer, mesoderm, which forms muscles, the coelom lining and most organs.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The coelom ladder:** acoelomate → pseudocoelomate → coelomate tracks increasing body complexity — room for organs, a hydrostatic skeleton and independent gut movement.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Levels: protoplasmic (Protozoa) → cellular (Porifera) → tissue (Cnidaria) → organ (Platyhelminthes) → organ-system (Annelida onward).  ·  Symmetry: asymmetrical (Porifera), radial (Cnidaria; secondary in adult Echinodermata), bilateral (Platyhelminthes onward).  ·  Germ layers: diploblastic (Cnidaria) vs triploblastic (onward). Body cavity: acoelomate (Platyhelminthes), pseudocoelomate (Aschelminthes), eucoelomate (Annelida onward).  ·  Protostomes (mouth from blastopore; spiral cleavage; schizocoely) vs deuterostomes (anus from blastopore; radial cleavage; enterocoely).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Bilateral symmetry with a head-tail axis is the body plan of the vast majority of animal species.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The body cavity fully lined by mesoderm is called: → C  ·  Cnidaria shows what type of symmetry? → B

rows.text: ## 1. Levels of Organization | Level | Description | Phyla | |---|---|---| | **Protoplasmic (protoplasmic grade)** | Unicellular; all functions in one cell | Protozoa (Protista) | | **Cellular** | Multicellular but little coordination; no true tissues | Porifera (sponges) | | **Tissue** | Cells organised into tissues | Cnidaria (Coelenterata) | | **Organ** | Tissues grouped…  ·  ## 3. Body Symmetry | Type | Description | Phyla | |---|---|---| | **Asymmetrical** | No plane divides the body into mirror halves | Most Porifera | | **Radial** | Any plane through the central axis gives mirror halves; suited to sessile or drifting life | Cnidaria, adult Echinodermata | | **Bilateral** | Only one plane (sagittal) divides into mirror halves; head-tail axis;…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Segmentation: true metamerism (Annelida), external with tagmatization (Arthropoda), vertebral (Chordata).  ·  Nematodes (roundworms) are pseudocoelomates; Annelida are coelomates.  ·  All chordates have a notochord at some stage; in vertebrates it is replaced by the vertebral column.
